full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J. :- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties No.1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 passed by the learned District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.102 of 2011 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 15.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st court, Barisal in Title Suit No.31 of 2009 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties No.1-10 as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No.31 of 2009 in the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Barisal for declaration of title in the land described in schedule 'kas of the plaint contending inter cilia, that the suit property appertaining to Mouza-Bogra Alekanda under J.L. No.50 of Police. Station and District-Barisal, corresponding to R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. khatian No.1987, in plotNo.5216 consists of an area .11 acres and .02 acres in plot No.5239 in all .13 acres of land originally belonged to one Nibaran Chandra Bar. Nibaran Chandra Bar during his life time had been owning and possessing the suit property and subsequently transferred the suit land in favour of his two sons Dipok Bar and Dilip Bar and grandsons Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar by an unregistered deed of gift dated 20.04.1979 and handed over possession to them. Subsequently; Nibaran Chandra died on 20.09.1980. Among the aforesaid gift holders, on 10.08.1981 Dilip Bar, Mikel P.K. Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their portion of land in favour of Dipak Bar by a deed of gift. Thereafter; Dipak Bar by virtue of a Mutation Case being No.593/1981-82 mutated his name in the Government 'Serest-a' and paying rents regularly for the suit property. Subsequently; Dipak Bar mortgaged .51/2 acres of land in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and in lieu of that; obtained loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. After taking loan keeping mortgage of some of the properties, Dipak Bar erected a semi-pakka dwelling house consists-of 03 bed rooms, kitchen and latrine therein and started to reside therein with his family members. Thereafter; Dipak Bar died leaving behind three sons namely the plaintiff No.1 Rupak Bar and the predecessor of the plaintiffs No.2-5 Mikel P.K. Bar and the predecessor of the plaintiff No.6 & 7 Pulak Bar with two daughters the plaintiff No.8 & 9 and one wife, the plaintiff No.10 and in this way the heirs of Dipak Bar use to reside in the suit homestead property after payment of the loan amount in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. It is the case of the plaintiffs that the 'defendants having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property, on the basis of false allegation claimed the suit property on 22.04.2008 and tried to mutate their names at which the title of the plaintiffs have been clouded and to dispel that cloud, they have instituted the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No.1, 2 and 4 in short is thus that the property-in-dispute originally belonged to Nibaran Chandra Bar and he died leaving behind his heirs two sons Dipak Bar and Dilip Bar with one daughter Era Bar and in this way the sons and daughter of the original owner became the owner of the suit property. After the death of Dilip Bar his one wife Saraj Bar and brother Dipak Bar and sister Era Bar became the owner and possessors of the suit property. The further case of the defendants is such that the wife of Dilip Bar died leaving behind three sons namely Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar with two daughters; the plaintiffs No.8 and 9. Subsequently, Pulak Bar died leaving behind his one daughter the plaintiff No.6 and one wife Jesika Bar and in this way the heirs and successive heirs of Dipak Bar used to possess the suit property. The plaintiffs No.1-5 with an ill-motive to deprive the defendants created two deed of gifts and in fact Nibaran Chandra Bar or Dilip Bar never executed any deed of gift as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs and as such the plaintiff's suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing 05 (five) different issues decided the issues on maintainability, limitation and defect of party in favour of the plaintiffs and decided the issue on right, title, interest and possession, against the plaintiffs and thereby dismissed the suit on 15.06.2011.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being No.102 of 2011 in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal which was heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge himself and by the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 the learned appellate court allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and decreed the suit on contest.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-respondent-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained this Rule with an interim order of status quo.

7. During hearing of this Rule, Mr. Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Md. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal misdirected himself in his total approach of the matter and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned District Judge, Barisal at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree failed to appreciate the exact proposition of law and also failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective. The learned Advocate also submits that admittedly the property-in-dispute originally belonged to Nibaran Chandra Bar and it is the positive contention of the plaintiffs that, by two deeds of gift, they have acquired the suit property and possessing the same, but the plaintiffs to the suit have failed to prove that the executants of the deeds in fact executed the deeds in favour of the donees and there is no direct evidence of possession in favour of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate argued that none of the plaintiff's witnesses have been able to prove the case of the plaintiffs and the P.Ws. are not competent, disinterested and trustworthy while the defendant's witnesses have successfully proved the case of the defendants and disproved the case of the plaintiffs, which is totally ignored by the learned appellate court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the trial court during disposal of the original suit rightly under the ambit of Order V, rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure after proper evaluation of the evidence on records dismissed the suit on contest. But the learned appellate court without reversing the findings of the trial court reversed the judgment and decree of the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law and facts.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit by adducing sufficient tangible, credible evidence both oral and documentary have successfully proved that they have acquired their valid right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by virtue of their deeds of gift and as successors of the original admitted owner Nibaran Chandra Bar and that the plaintiffs to the suit after acquiring the suit property possessing the same after mutating their names in the government `seresta' and by regular payment of rents to the government. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court during disposal of the original suit decided in his judgment and decree that the suit in its present form is maintainable and there is no legal bar of institution of the original suit and the learned Joint District Judge, 1' Court, Barisal also decided conclusively that the suit is not barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties. The only point for dismissal the suit was such by the learned trial court that the title and interest of the suit property is not proved from the side of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate argued that against the observation and decisions of the trial court on point of limitation, defect of party and maintainability, the defendants did not file any appeal or cross-objection and thereby it is the proposition of law that they have admitted that findings and decisions of the trial court which is apparently against them. The leaned Advocate submits that the deeds of gift as contended from the side of the plaintiffs in their pleading, has been duly proved and those were exhibited under the provisions of Evidence Act without any objection. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in the year 1979 there was no provision that the unregistered deed of gift is not valid in the eye of law and the learned trial court is totally misconceived in holding the view that the title documents of the plaintiffs are not proved. The learned Advocate in his submissions categorically pointed out the evidence on records and submits that the learned appellate court at the time of deciding the merit of the appeal rightly after proper sifting of evidence and assessment of the same in its true perspective on proper appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and rebutted the findings of the trial court, adverting evidence on records and thereafter; reversed the findings and judgment passed by the trial court and in the impugned judgment and decree there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with.

10. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned counsels, having gone through the respective cases of the parties and the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court as well as the appellate court in consultation with the evidence on records and the pleadings of the parties it transpires that the suit property appertaining to Mouza Bogra Alekanda under Barisal Sadar Upazila corresponding to R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. Khatian No.1987 in plot No.5216 of the S.A. khatian No.1987 consists of an area 0.11 acres and .02 acres of S.A. plot No.5239 in all .13 acres of land originally belonged to one Nibaran Chandra Bar. Nibaran Chandra Bar during his life time had been owning and possessing the suit property and thereafter transferred the suit land in favour of his two sons Dipok Bar and Dilip Bar and grandsons Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar by an unregistered deed of gift dated 20.04.1979, which was written on 19.04.1979. It was further contention of the plaintiffs that the admitted owner of the property after execution of the deed of gift handed over possession of the suit property in favour of the aforesaid 05 donees. Subsequently; by another deed of gift dated 10.08.1981 Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulok Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their share in favour of Dipak Bar. The aforesaid two deeds of gift have been marked as Exhibit-7 and 7(ka) after its formal proof. by the attesting witness of the deeds P.W.2 Pal Sarnendu Sarker, who in fact proved the deeds dated 20.04.1979 and 10.08.1981. It further transpires from the papers on records that the plaintiffs in order to prove their case have produced the R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. Khatian No.1987 which has been marked as Exhibit No.2 and 3 respectively. Besides this; the Mutation Khatian No.16008 and the paper relating to Mutation Case No.593KT/81-82 has also been produced from the side of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land and these papers have been marked as Exhibit-4 and 5 respectively by which the plaintiff Dipak Bar have mutated his name in the government `seresia. The subsequent payment of rents in respect of the suit property followed by rent receipts were also produced from the side of the plaintiffs to substantiate their case. With regard to taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation by Dipak Bar, the mortgage papers in respect of .5Y2 acres of land has been marked as Exhibit-2 by the trial court and it is the positive case of the plaintiffs in their pleadings that after taking loan, their predecessor have erected a semi-pacca dwelling house in the suit property and started to reside therein. The plaintiff's predecessor Dipak Bar opened a separate khatian in the government `seresta' and after payment of rent obtained rent receipt which is Exhibit-1.

11. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records I find that the specific assertion of the plaintiffs that the son of Nibaron Chandra namely Dilip Bar was unmarried and on the contrary it is the case of the contesting defendants that the witness No.2 of the defendants namely Soraj Bar is the married wife of Dilip Bar.

12. To substantiate the respective cases of the parties, 04 witnesses were produced from the side of the plaintiffs and 03 witnesses from the side of the defendants.

13. P.W.1 is the plaintiff No.9 who is the daughter of Dipak Bar namely Orpa Bar. This witness deposed on behalf of all the plaintiffs. In her testimony, she has categorically testified that her grandfather Nibaron Chandra Bar was the original owner of the suit property and his grandfather gifted the property in favour of his sons Dipak Bar, Dilip Bar and three grand sons. In the said deed of gift of 20.04.1979 the witnesses were the Secretary of Baptist Church namely Smith Biswas and the President/Proctor of YMCA. P.W.1 further testified in her deposition that Dilip Bar subsequently by another deed of gift dated 10.08.1981 transferred his share in favour of his brother Dipok Bar. On the same date the 03 donees of the earlier gift deed, Mike! P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their share in favour of Dipak Bar and Dipak Bar in a mutation proceedings mutated his name and opened a separate khatian. He also paid rent for the suit property. The plaintiff No.9 to substantiate the pleadings of the plaintiffs also testified that her father Dipak Bar after taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation erected a dwelling house consists of 03 rooms and used to reside therein with his family members.

During cross-examination from the side of the defendants the witness No.1 of the plaintiffs in a reply to a question testified that, it is the fact that the suit property was acquired by two sons of Nibaran Chandra and one daughter Era Bar. This witness in her deposition in a reply to another question from the side of the contesting defendants testified that they have filed the mortgage deed of 16.08.1982 which is in respect of taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. This paper has been marked as Exhibit-6, and the plaintiffs have also submitted the Poura Tax receipt vide Exhibit-7.

14. P.W.2 is the attesting witness of the deeds of gift, Pal Sarnindu Sarker. This witness in his testimony testified in support of the deeds of gift dated 20.04.1979 and 10.08.1981. He has identified his signatures in serial NO.6 of the deed of 1979 and serial No.1 of the deed of 1981.

During cross-examination this witness specifically testified about his presence at the time of delivery of possession and presence of other two witnesses who were 7/8 in numbers.

15. P.W.3 is one Kamol Sarker, who is another attesting witness of the deed of gift dated 10.08.1981. This witness identified his signature as attesting witness of the deed in serial No.2. From his cross-examination it appears that at the relevant time he was a teacher of Baptist Mission School and Secretary of the Church.

16. The last witness of the plaintiffs is P.W.4 A.T.M. Shahidullah, who is a Ward Councilor of Barisal City Corporation No.10. This witness in his testimony testifies that he knows the suit land, in where the plaintiffs are residing as of their homestead and in the said property the defendants have no possession. P.W.4 in his deposition categorically testified that in his area the defendants are not the voters, but the plaintiffs are voters. As to the identity of the suit property the witness No.4 deposed that the suit land is north-south long and in the northern side of the suit property some dwelling huts lies. P.W.4 also testified in his testimony that the defendants are not the residents of the suit Ward No.10 and they are the residents of Ward No.11 and both the two wards are adjacent.

17. Vis-à-vis; the witness No.1 of the defendants is the defendant No.4 Hiya Moni Sarker. This witness in her deposition testified that her mother's father is Nibaran Chandra Bar, who had three sons and one daughter, Rupak, Dilip, Dipak and her (D.W.1) mother Era Bar, who obtained 1/3 share in the suit property. D. W.1 further testified that Dilip Bar was married and his wife is Soraj Bar. After the death of her (D. W.1) mother the defendants No.1-5 became her heirs.

During cross-examination from the side of the plaintiffs D.W.1 frankly admitted that her residence is in Ward No.11 and the plaintiff's residence is situated in Ward No.10. This witness expressed her inability to state as to whether Nibaran Chandra Bar had signature in the deed of gift dated 19.04.1979. This witness also admitted in her testimony that the persons namely S. Biswas, Samir Adhikari, Sudhir Kumar Sarker and Probir Guha of the concerned locality are good and the defendants did not lodge any objection against the record. This witness in her testimony did not deny the building of Rupak Bar, but testifies that she does not know the area of the building and lastly this witness Hiya Moni Sarker frankly admits in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiffs that they did not file any case against the deeds of gift of the plaintiffs.

18. D.W.2 Soraj Bar testified in her testimony that Nibaran Bar was her father-in-law and in the year 1982 she married Dilip Bar at Dhaka Eskaton Church. This witness admits that the plaintiffs are the sons of her husband's brother.

During cross-examination, D.W.2 admitted at a stage that she worked as nurse at Barisal Baptist Mission Girl's School and in the school, she gave her address, which is different with her present address.

19. The last witness of the defendants D.W.3 Florence Mitra Karmakar is the Head Mistress of Barishal Baptist Mission Girl's High School. This witness in her deposition deposed that in her school, a lady namely Soraj Bar served, and her husband's name is Dilip Kumar Bar. This witness gave a certificate to that effect which has been marked as Exhibit-`ka'.

During cross-examination from the side of the plaintiffs, D.W.3 testified at a stage that she ever did not find the husband of Soraj Bar and also did not find the certificate of their marriage, but she knows that in that certificate the address of Dilip Bar was mentioned at New Eskaton. This witness in her cross-examination frankly admits that, in the certificate the address which was given by D.W.2 Soroj Bar is not same with the address of New Eskaton.

<u>20. On anxious consideration and assessment of mine on the evidence as adduced from the sides of the respective parties, I find that the learned appellate court in his observation and findings categorically adverting evidence on records reversed the findings of the trial court as to the right, title, interest and possession of the parties and after proper evaluation of the evidences, both oral and documentary, arrived at a conclusive decision that the plaintiffs to the suit have successfully discharged their onus in proving their respective case and there is no cogent and trustworthy evidence, which can be relied on from the side of the defendants to falsify the case of the plaintiffs. Under the ambit of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned appellate court elaborately discussed the evidence on records in its true perspective and thereafter decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellants therein. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from any sort of illegality or infirmity. Relying upon two decisions reported in 29 DLR 239 and 2 ADC 211, the learned District Judge, Barisal rightly decided the points in hands and the matter of adverse possession and hence, I find no ambiguity or misquoting of the provision of law as alleged from the side of the present petitioners, in the impugned judgment and decree. As to the acquisition of the right, title, interest and possession in the suit property the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs led me to draw such inference that in the suit property the plaintiffs have acquired a valid right, title, interest and they are possessing the same.</u>

<u>21. It is to be remembered that, under section 49 of the Registration Act [XVI of 1908], a document which is required to be registered under this Act, but not registered, yet be admitted for collateral purposes, as to prove the nature of possession and such an ancient document can be used to prove acquisition of title by adverse possession in appropriate cases.</u>

22. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule has got no merit to succeed.

23. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 passed by the learned District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.102 of 2011 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 15.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1 st court, Barisal in Title Suit No.31 of 2009 dismissing the suit is hereby affirmed.

24. The order of status quo granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

25. However, there will be no order as to costs.

26. Send back the Lower Court's Records and communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.
